summary: The temple-state of the Zilin Hills: a pious public face and a hidden council behind it; two-face focuses whose true names appear after the reveal.

temple_state.name: The Temple-State of Zilin
temple_state.desc: Three hill valleys under the rule of a temple. Its people are devout, its pilgrims are many and its soldiers are few.

pilgrim_roads_spirit.name: The Pilgrim Roads
pilgrim_roads_spirit.desc: Mended roads and wayhouses link the Hermitage to every land. Pilgrims arrive with news, silver and goodwill.

scriptorium.name: The Hermitage Scriptorium
scriptorium.desc: Monks copy the scrolls of the temple, the histories of the Ages and the letters of pilgrims.

healers_of_zilin_spirit.name: Healers of Zilin
healers_of_zilin_spirit.desc: The healers of the Hermitage treat the poor for nothing, and the hill valleys are known for their health.

open_letters.name: Letters to Every Court
open_letters.desc: A letter from the Hermitage reaches every court in Aoaz, polite and signed with a blessing.

guardians_of_the_hills_spirit.name: Guardians of the Hills
guardians_of_the_hills_spirit.desc: A small guard of the Hermitage holds the hilltops and the roads. They are trained to defend and not to attack.

deliverers_peace.name: The Deliverer's Peace
deliverers_peace.desc: The Deliverer's peace is preached from every pulpit and kept at every gate. The Hermitage seeks no war.

great_almonry.name: The Great Almonry
great_almonry.desc: The alms of the Houses are gathered in one hand and spent where the need is greatest.

houses_without_number_spirit.name: Houses Without Number
houses_without_number_spirit.desc: There is a House of the First Light in every city, a ward in every hospital and a lamp in every window.

couriers.name: Pilgrim Couriers
couriers.desc: Pilgrims carry letters from city to city and are the best-informed travellers in Aoaz.

every_road.name: Every Road a Pilgrim Road
every_road.desc: Every road of Aoaz is linked by an unbroken line of wayhouses, and news travels faster than any courier.

hymns.name: Hymns of Deliverance
hymns.desc: Choirs sing the Hymns in the great hall and at the gates. The tunes are simple and easily learned, and they spread.

doctrine_of_deliverance_spirit.name: The Doctrine of Deliverance
doctrine_of_deliverance_spirit.desc: The doctrine is written in plain words and taught in every temple school. It is gentle, sure and very hard to refute.

radiant_face.name: The Radiant Face
radiant_face.desc: The Deliverer's face is radiant and mild. The faithful weep to see it, and the doubters fall quiet.

palace_wards.name: Wards of the Palace
palace_wards.desc: Wards, seals and bolted doors surround the palace at Parim, and the outer halls are open to pilgrims.

crowned_deliverer.name: The Throne Blessed
crowned_deliverer.desc: The throne of Aenor is blessed, and the new king is anointed with balm. The court is pleased, and the temples are full.

new_god_of_men_spirit.name: New God of Men
new_god_of_men_spirit.desc: The faithful raise their eyes to the throne and see a king who is more than a king. The priests do not correct them.

parim_shall_not_fall_spirit.name: Parim Shall Not Fall
parim_shall_not_fall_spirit.desc: The city will not fall. The faithful gather within its walls, and the garrison fights with a hard, calm resolve.

endless_regency.name: A Wise Regency
endless_regency.desc: A wise regency governs in the king's name, and the realm is calm, orderly and very quiet.

eastern_throne.name: Banners of the Dawn
eastern_throne.desc: The banners of the dawn lands are raised at the Hermitage. The host that gathers beneath them is devoted and orderly.

eastern_fleets.name: Ships of the Eastern Seas
eastern_fleets.desc: Ships from the eastern harbours are fitted out for a long voyage, with volunteer crews and sealed orders.

host_of_the_east.name: The Gathered Faithful
host_of_the_east.desc: The faithful of the East march beneath banners of white and gold, singing as they go.

fear_and_worship_spirit.name: Awe of the Faithful
fear_and_worship_spirit.desc: The temples are packed, the streets are quiet and the people cannot tell awe from fear.

gods_court.name: The God's Court
gods_court.desc: The Houses are restored in every land, with new gifts, new wards and new patrons. The court that sits above them is not of this world.

pilgrims_at_the_gate.title: Pilgrims at the Gate
pilgrims_at_the_gate.desc: A long line of pilgrims waits at the gate of the Hermitage, hungry, footsore and singing. The keepers ask whether they should be fed first or blessed first.

options.name: Bless them and send them home.

envoys_of_many_crowns.title: Envoys of Many Crowns
envoys_of_many_crowns.desc: Envoys of a dozen courts have arrived at the Hermitage in a single week. The keepers do not wish to offend any of them, but there is only one chair at the head of the table.

quiet_borders.title: The Hermitage Asks for Quiet Borders
quiet_borders.desc: Pilgrims from the Hermitage have come to the elven forest bearing gifts and a letter. The Hermitage asks for quiet borders and open roads, and promises in return the friendship of its prayers.

options.name: The elves keep their own counsel.

leren_mood.title: The Mood of the Leren Court
leren_mood.desc: Your couriers have returned from the court of Sonargur. The sea-kings are proud, restless and unhappy with their treaty. They will say as much to anyone who listens.

report_from_the_passes.title: Report from the Passes
report_from_the_passes.desc: Pilgrims returned from Mirolon with an account of the passes, the garrisons and a storm that never seems to move. They are certain that the walls are watched by something more than men.

letter_from_merovan.title: A Letter from Merovan
letter_from_merovan.desc: The keeper of the royal seals has written again. His letter is long, courteous and full of small requests. At its end he asks to be remembered to the Deliverer.

reliquary_inventory.title: The Reliquary Inventory
reliquary_inventory.desc: The keepers of the reliquary have finished their inventory. It lists the Necklace of the Abyss and three lesser pieces, each of which is attuned to one hand alone.

guest_who_does_not_age.title: The Guest Who Does Not Age
guest_who_does_not_age.desc: A stranger has come to the reliquary, a pleasant man who looks no older than he did on the day he first came. He asks nothing, and he knows the name of every relic in the vault.

options.name: Give him a chair in the Council.

what_council_knows.title: What the Council Knows of Yeldenne
what_council_knows.desc: Your listeners report that a green light has been seen at night above a castle in the north. A single man is said to watch it from the battlements.

options.name: Leave it until there is cause.

servants_beyond_veil.title: Servants Beyond the Veil
servants_beyond_veil.desc: The servants beyond the veil have heard the summons and have come. They stand in the courtyard of the Hermitage without speaking, and the pilgrims have been sent indoors.

a_keeper_for_the_hermitage.title: A Keeper for the Hermitage
a_keeper_for_the_hermitage.desc: The Hermitage will be kept while the Deliverer reigns. The High Confessor has agreed to take the keys, the gates and the granaries, and the faithful are glad of it.

quiet_court.title: The Quiet Court
quiet_court.desc: The old king still sits upon his throne, signs what is placed before him and sees the people his counsellors wish him to see. He never knew, and he never will.

quiet_court_heir.title: The Quiet Court of the Child
quiet_court_heir.desc: A child sits on the throne of Aenor with a tutor at his ear and a regent at his shoulder. The court is calm, and the child is happy.

effects.tooltip: The faithful pray for the King.
A vigil is kept for the King.

elves_declined.name: The Elves Kept Their Own Counsel

focuses.name: The Hermitage of Zilin
focuses.desc: In the Zilin Hills a temple-state keeps its gates open to every pilgrim, every beggar and every wandering scholar. The Hermitage begins by feeding those who come and by turning no one away.

focuses.name: Mend the Pilgrim Roads
focuses.desc: The roads that lead to the Hermitage are mended stone by stone. Wayhouses are built at every day's journey, and pilgrims bless the name of the temple that built them.

focuses.name: The Alms of the Faithful
focuses.desc: The faithful of the Deliverer give freely. Their alms are sorted and counted at the temple door and spent on grain, medicine and mending.

focuses.name: Granaries of the Three Valleys
focuses.desc: Three valleys send their harvests to the temple granaries, which stand full in the leanest year. The Hermitage has never been hungry.

focuses.name: The Hermitage Scriptorium
focuses.desc: In the scriptorium monks copy the scrolls of the temple, the old histories of the Ages and the letters of pilgrims. A good copyist is worth more than a good soldier here.

focuses.name: Healers of Zilin
focuses.desc: The healers of Zilin are known in every court. They treat the poor for nothing and the rich for a fair fee, and none of them has ever been seen to refuse a patient.

focuses.name: Temple Masons
focuses.desc: The temple masons raise walls, bridges and tall halls from the red stone of the hills. Their work is simple and does not fall down.

focuses.name: Letters to Every Court
focuses.desc: A letter goes to every court in Aoaz in the Hermitage's own hand. It is polite, unthreatening and signed with a blessing.

focuses.name: The Open Door
focuses.desc: The gates of the Hermitage are never closed. Envoys, merchants and pilgrims of every crown walk in and are fed.

focuses.name: Guardians of the Hills
focuses.desc: A small guard is raised to keep the roads safe and the temple unmolested. They carry staves and spears and are trained to defend, never to attack.

focuses.name: Friends Among the Elves
focuses.desc: The Hermitage lies close to the elven forest, and the Deliverer has always sought the friendship of its wardens. Gifts and messages are exchanged in the old way.

focuses.name: Hill Wardens
focuses.desc: Watch-towers rise on the hilltops and the gates are fitted with iron. The Hermitage has no enemies, but it is wise not to be careless.

focuses.name: The Deliverer's Peace
focuses.desc: The Deliverer's peace is preached from every pulpit and kept at every gate. It is the Hermitage's great gift to Aoaz, and its great ambition.

focuses.name: The Houses of the First Light
focuses.desc: The Houses of the First Light are halls of charity: hostels for the poor, schools for orphans and wards for the sick. They open wherever a patron can be found to pay for their lamps.

focuses.name: Grain of Charity
focuses.desc: Carts of grain leave the Hermitage for the hungry quarters of distant cities. Wherever they stop, a House of the First Light is soon to follow.

focuses.name: Physicians of the Houses
focuses.desc: Physicians in white robes are sent to the Houses, and the poor are treated without payment. A grateful patient remembers the hand that healed him.

focuses.name: Keepers of the Birth Rolls
focuses.desc: The Houses keep rolls of births, deaths and marriages for any family that asks. A parish that trusts the rolls trusts the keepers of them.

focuses.name: The Hospitals of Parim
focuses.desc: A great hospital rises in Parim, with a hundred beds and a physician for every ten. The royal court is generous and the physicians are grateful.

focuses.name: Chairs at the Universities
focuses.desc: The temple endows chairs at the universities of Selen and beyond. A scholar fed by the temple teaches what the temple would like taught.

focuses.name: Houses in the North
focuses.desc: In the harsh cold of the North Lands the Houses are warmer than the inns and cheaper than the alehouses. Sailors of Lerendor learn to go there first.

focuses.name: Houses Across the Sea
focuses.desc: Ships carry grain, bandages and sisters of the temple across the western sea. The Houses of the West are the first to open their doors to the wounded of the Gunwaith wars.

focuses.name: Houses on the Caravan Roads
focuses.desc: Wayhouses on the eastern caravan roads give water to the camel-men and soup to the drivers. The caravan houses are well pleased and say so.

focuses.name: Houses of the Islands
focuses.desc: Fishermen, sailors and island farmers receive the Houses gladly. The sisters learn the island tongues and sing at the island festivals.

focuses.name: Houses Under the Sun
focuses.desc: The Houses open under the white-gold sun of the elven kingdoms. Their sisters learn what the elves already know and keep their counsel.

focuses.name: The Famine Stores
focuses.desc: The Hermitage sets aside stores of grain for the worst years. In the hungry season a House with an open granary is a House beloved.

focuses.name: The Great Almonry
focuses.desc: The Great Almonry gathers the alms of the Houses into one hand and spends them where the need is greatest. It is the largest charity in Aoaz.

focuses.name: Debts of Gratitude
focuses.desc: A man who has been fed remembers it. The Houses keep no accounts, but they keep a memory of who owes them what.

focuses.name: Houses Without Number
focuses.desc: There is a House of the First Light in every city, a ward in every hospital and a lamp in every window. The Deliverer's name is spoken in all of them.

effects.tooltip: Corvel may be hired as an advisor.

focuses.name: Pilgrim Couriers
focuses.desc: Pilgrims carry letters from city to city and are glad of the Hermitage's hospitality. They are the best-informed travellers in Aoaz.

focuses.name: Confessors at Foreign Courts
focuses.desc: The Hermitage sends confessors to foreign courts to hear the troubles of kings and the burdens of queens. They listen very well.

focuses.name: The Ledger of Debts
focuses.desc: The Hermitage keeps a ledger of the favours it has done for the great and the small. The ledger is never consulted, but it is never lost either.

focuses.name: Gifts to the Eastern Kings
focuses.desc: Gifts of silk, grain and holy balm are sent to the courts of the East. Each is chosen with care and presented with a blessing.

focuses.name: The Long Courtship
focuses.desc: A patient courtship of the eastern crowns, with letters, gifts and understanding, begins to bear fruit. A king who has been courted for a decade finds it hard to refuse a friend.

focuses.name: Counsellors from the Houses
focuses.desc: Counsellors trained in the Houses are recommended to the royal court. They are honest, diligent and very well informed.

effects.tooltip: Ilvane may be hired as an advisor.

focuses.name: Hymns of Deliverance
focuses.desc: Choirs of the Hermitage sing the Hymns of Deliverance in the great hall and at the gates. The tunes are simple and easily learned, and they spread.

focuses.name: Miracles at the Wells
focuses.desc: It is said that the wells of the Hermitage never run dry and that the sick who drink from them are healed. Pilgrims by the thousand come to see.

focuses.name: Tutors for Princes
focuses.desc: The Hermitage offers tutors to the princes of far courts. A prince taught by the temple is a prince who loves it.

focuses.name: Remember the Jubilee
focuses.desc: The Thousand-Year Jubilee of 4A 1000 is remembered in the royal court of Aenor, with hymns, torches and the solemn reading of old oaths.

focuses.name: Renew the Thousand Oaths
focuses.desc: The oaths sworn on the Jubilee are renewed in every temple. The faithful kneel, the choirs sing, and a hundred thousand voices repeat the old words.

focuses.name: The Doctrine of Deliverance
focuses.desc: The doctrine of the Deliverer is written out in plain words and taught in every temple school. It is gentle, sure and nearly impossible to refute.

focuses.name: The Reliquary Vaults
focuses.desc: The temple's reliquary is a vault of stone, iron and oak, kept under three keys. Its inventory is old, long and known to very few.

focuses.name: The Thief's Errands
focuses.desc: A trusted servant of the Hermitage travels the roads on errands too small to be noticed. He is cheerful, courteous and impossible to describe afterward.

focuses.name: Maps of the Cold Coast
focuses.desc: Mapmakers of the Hermitage copy the charts of the northern coasts and mark the passes, the anchorages and the ice. Pilgrims who go north will have maps.

focuses.name: Wards of the Palace
focuses.desc: Wards, seals and bolted doors are set around the palace at Parim. Pilgrims are still welcome in the outer halls, but the inner ones are barred.

focuses.name: A Keeper for the Hermitage
focuses.desc: A trusted keeper is named for the Hermitage, to hold its gates and its granaries while the Deliverer sits upon a throne in the Middle Lands.

focuses.name: The Seal-Keeper's Charge
focuses.desc: The royal seal-keeper is charged with the rule of the realm during the Deliverer's absences. Aenor must run smoothly while its king is away.

focuses.name: Denounce the Impostor
focuses.desc: A stranger claims royal blood and slanders the Deliverer. The crown calls him what he is: an impostor.

focuses.name: New God of Men
focuses.desc: The faithful of Aenor raise their eyes to the throne and see a king who is more than a king. The priests do not correct them.

focuses.name: The Quiet Court
focuses.desc: The throne of Aenor has not changed hands, and nothing seems to have changed in the palace. Counsellors come and go in the Hermitage's white, and the court goes on as it always has.

focuses.name: Keepers of the Crown
focuses.desc: The crown's keepers are the temple's men. The royal edicts are drafted at the Hermitage and signed in Parim.

focuses.name: A Kingdom Without War
focuses.desc: Aenor is at peace and Aoaz is at peace. If the world is quiet long enough, no one will remember that it was ever otherwise.

effects.tooltip: Counts toward the proposed outcome of a surviving Golden Court.

focuses.name: Roads to the Dawn
focuses.desc: The long courtship of the East is made plain. The Hermitage declares that it has friends in every eastern court and that those friends will receive it.

focuses.name: Ships of the Eastern Seas
focuses.desc: Ships from the eastern harbours are fitted out for a long voyage. Their crews are volunteers, and their captains are given sealed orders.

focuses.name: The God's Palace
focuses.desc: The palace at Parim is made a fortress of the faith. Its wards are renewed and its gates are guarded by the faithful.
